summary: Reproduced the reported unfused scaled-FP8 KV write in the actual MHATokenToKVPool implementation: one relevant BF16 store kernel versus five scaled-FP8 kernels and a 1.88x pool-call latency ratio on the assigned gfx950. No duplicate fix was implemented because active upstream PR #31652 already provides the CUDA candidate and was reconfirmed active on 2026-09-12.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual pool-level batch-1 KV writes on MI350X gfx950: BF16 median 24.88 us with one relevant store kernel; scaled FP8 median 46.72 us with two divide, two cast, and one store kernels. K and V were bit-exact against an independent PyTorch divide-then-cast reference. Raw output: reports/j-2a14448cfa2f/reproduce_fp8_kv_write.log.

Existing cache-store and pool boundary coverage: 366 tests passed with 9 subtests, including batch sizes, row widths, index dtypes, split configurations, asymmetric K/V dimensions, prefix-valid guards, and untouched-slot checks. Raw output: reports/j-2a14448cfa2f/focused_tests.log.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, reported by PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; profiler device event names and numerical results are retained in reports/j-2a14448cfa2f/reproduce_fp8_kv_write.log.

remaining_limitations: The assigned GPU is AMD gfx950, not the reported Hopper H200/SM90, so H200/FA3 end-to-end decode slowdown was not reproduced or claimed.
No full model weights were available or required for the isolated KV-write path; no model-level ITL or semantic-accuracy claim is made.
The per-layer FA3 query conversion and FA3 split-KV performance claims remain unverified without FA3-capable Hopper hardware.
Active upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31652 is CUDA-only and leaves ROCm unfused; it was inspected but not duplicated or modified.
